1.12 Preserve exact original files

The historical filename preserve_apo.py now accepts explicit generic roots:

uv run python preserve_apo.py scan SOURCE REFERENCE ARCHIVE
    [--project DIRECTORY] [--workers N] [--rate-mib N]
    [--full-copy] [--delta]
uv run python preserve_apo.py restore ARCHIVE RELATIVE_PATH OUTPUT
    [--reference-root DIRECTORY]

The scan inventories all regular files, not just DNGs, and rejects unsupported file entries such as symlinks. It uses any supplied known-pair ledger and otherwise looks for the same relative path under the reference. An absent reference is preserved as a complete original. Keep source/reference roots stable, writable output separate, and one archive owner at a time.

Mode Equal whole-file bytes Different bytes with reference Missing reference
Default SHA-bound reference Complete original Complete original
--delta SHA-bound reference Verified VCDIFF delta Complete original
--full-copy Complete original Complete original Complete original

--full-copy takes precedence over delta storage. The scan compares complete source/reference bytes, records their SHA-256, validates before/after identities, and rereads saved complete originals. For a delta, xdelta3 encodes the source version against the reference. The archive then decodes it and requires the reconstructed SHA to equal the observed source SHA. VCDIFF is a standard delta format, rather than an image-specific edit representation. RFC 3284.

The scan records source attributes, including mode, times and extended attributes where supported. A restore verifies payload bytes before a no-overwrite commit and reapplies saved xattrs, mode and times. It does not recreate every possible filesystem property: saved uid/gid/flags are not all automatically restored. Cross-platform xattr support also differs. Preserve that distinction from an exact file-payload guarantee.

The public entry points reject an archive output that overlaps a source or reference root. This protects against writing recovery files into the trees being audited. It does not supply an automatic cross-process lock to every low-level API. Use one archive owner and separate output directories.

summary.json distinguishes processed completion, errors and byte_preservation_complete. recovery.sqlite3 is the checkpoint, manifest.jsonl is the portable record view, inventory.json covers source files, and directories.json retains directory attributes. Each recovery record says whether it uses original, delta or a reference alone. The scan never sets safe_to_delete_source true by itself.

Default and delta archives depend on retained exact reference bytes. An XMP write can break that dependency despite unchanged samples. Keep another independent reference copy, archive the reference too, or choose full-copy storage. Restore can accept a relocated reference root through --reference-root; the relative reference path must be safe and the bytes must still match the recorded hash. An existing output is rejected, so restore into a new location.
